content.text: I found three live message families using the same banner style: session-start linkage, “no commits yet”, and the fallback “tracking enabled but Entire CLI missing.” I’m reading the exact constructors so the wording proposal can stay consistent across one-line and multi-line agent formats.
The biggest product choice is whether to keep a branded banner at all or switch to plain product voice. That decision will affect every hook message, tests, and docs.

questions.question: Which direction should the hook messages follow?

options.description: Drop "Powered by Entire" and start directly with "Entire CLI..." for clearer, more natural wording.

options.label: Keep banner
options.description: Retain "Powered by Entire:" as a prefix, but rewrite the sentence after it.

options.label: Short label
options.description: Use a lighter prefix like "Entire:" and keep the rest concise.

content.text:
I’d move to direct product voice and drop `Powered by Entire:` entirely.

Recommended style:
- Start with `Entire CLI ...`
- Use active voice
- Say exactly what happens
- Avoid “powered by” phrasing, which reads like attribution rather than instruction

Proposed rewrites for the current messages:

- `Entire CLI will link this conversation to your next commit.`
- `Entire CLI will start linking checkpoints after your first commit.`
- `Entire CLI tracking is enabled, but the Entire CLI is not installed or not on your PATH. Installation guide: https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation#installation-methods`

If you want them slightly tighter, I’d use:
- `Entire CLI will link this conversation to your next commit.`
- `Make your first commit to start using Entire CLI checkpoints.`
- `Entire CLI tracking is enabled, but the CLI is not installed or not on your PATH. Installation guide: https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation#installation-methods`

My recommendation is the first set. It’s clearer and keeps the wording parallel across all hook messages.

If you want, next I can turn this into a full message style guide for all hook/system messages in the repo, including tone rules and exact replacement strings.
